svg.title: Simpson's paradox: exercise vs. cholesterol
svg.desc: Pearl's example where age is a confounder. Right: pooled data of cholesterol (Y) against exercise (X) shows a positive trend. Left: the same data split by age group (10, 20, 30, 40, 50); within each age group, more exercise goes with lower cholesterol (each group's line slopes down), while older groups both exercise more and have higher cholesterol.
